captions.detailed: This 3D model is a partial wheel-shaped cable-pulling servo horn, spanning a sector of approximately 120 degrees. It features a continuous V-shaped groove along its curved outer rim for guiding a cable or line. Near the apex of the sector, there is a counterbored mounting hole containing a female spline pattern designed to press-fit onto a servo motor shaft. Two small diagonal tie-off holes are drilled near the flat ends of the curved rim to secure the cable ends.
captions.instruction: Create a parametric cable-pulling servo horn in OpenSCAD. The design should allow the user to adjust the sweep angle, wheel diameter, wheel height, cable notch depth, and servo spline parameters, featuring a grooved outer rim, a splined servo mount hole, and integrated cable tie-off holes.
captions.factory: The script constructs the main body by taking a cylinder of wheel_radius, subtracting a pie-slice using a custom cut_pie module, and unioning it with a central servo mount cylinder and tangential filler cubes to smooth the transition. A V-shaped groove is cut into the curved rim using rotate_extrude with a polygon profile. The internal female spline is subtracted using a custom servomount module consisting of a splinewheel (generated by looping tooth polygons) and concentric cylinders for screw and counterbore clearances. Finally, two angled cylinders are subtracted near the flat ends to form the cable tie-off holes.
